name: Louis Armstrong
hook: New Orleans' trumpet king, from the Hot Five to "Hello, Dolly!"

facts.label: New Orleans
facts.statement: Louis Armstrong was born in New Orleans, which named its airport for him and held a centennial Jazz Fest in 2001.

facts.label: "Hello, Dolly!"
facts.statement: In May 1964 his "Hello, Dolly!" knocked the Beatles' "Can't Buy Me Love" off No. 1; he was 62.

facts.label: "What a Wonderful World"
facts.statement: "What a Wonderful World," co-written by George Weiss, became a hit for him in 1967 and reached the Top 40 again in 1988.

facts.label: "When the Saints Go Marching In"
facts.statement: He recorded "When the Saints Go Marching In" in 1938; it is played at every New Orleans Saints home game.

facts.label: the cornet
facts.statement: Armstrong became famous on the trumpet but started on the cornet, its close brass relative.

facts.label: jazz
facts.statement: Asked what jazz is, he replied, "Man, if you gotta ask, you'll never know."

facts.label: July 4, 1900
facts.statement: He said he was born on the Fourth of July in 1900; later research pointed to August 4, 1901.
